title: Relative affine-line weight step
statement:
For the projection $p:\mathbf A^1_{Y_0}\to Y_0$ and every
$K\in D_{\le w}(\mathbf A^1_{Y_0})$, one has
$Rp_!K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-sheaves-to-complexes]. It says that, for a separated finite-type map, the complex upper-weight assertion follows once every mixed Weil sheaf of weights at most $v$ has $R^a p_!$ mixed of weights at most $v+a$ for every $a$. Thus it is enough to prove this sheaf-level assertion for the relative affine-line projection $p$.

source.place: Proof, opening reduction to the sheaf assertion

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F$ be mixed of weights at most $v$. By [def-weil-punctual-weights], it has a finite filtration by constructible Weil subsheaves whose successive quotients are punctually pure of weights at most $v$. The coefficient clause of [lem-zl-morphism-open-closed-reduction] propagates a direct-image bound through every finite filtration, and the extension estimate [lem-a1-extension-bounds] is the stalkwise weight step used in the long exact sequences. It therefore suffices to prove the sheaf bound for one punctually pure graded piece.

source.place: Proof, finite weight filtration and extension reduction

proof.text: For a punctually pure graded piece, apply [thm-zl-relative-line-stratification]. It gives finite source and target stratifications on which the sheaf is lisse and each induced map is either separated quasi-finite or smooth with one-dimensional affine geometric fibers. On a smooth relative-curve stratum, [thm-zl-relative-affine-curve-core] gives that $R^a p_!\mathcal F$ is mixed of weights at most $v+a$; on a separated quasi-finite stratum, [lem-zl-quasi-finite] gives the same upper-weight bound. Restricting a punctually pure sheaf to a stratum preserves that purity by the definition in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. When a stratum map is viewed as a composite with its locally closed target immersion, [lem-zl-shriek-composition] identifies the resulting exceptional direct image with the corresponding stratumwise piece of $Rp_!$.

The finite source and target stratifications can be ordered as successive open--closed decompositions. Apply the source and target clauses of [lem-zl-morphism-open-closed-reduction] inductively to reassemble the sheaf-level direct-image bounds from the stratumwise bounds. The corresponding localization triangles are glued at the complex level by [lem-zl-open-closed-weight]. Combining this reassembly with Step 1 yields $Rp_!K\in D_{\leq w}(Y_0)$ for every $K\in D_{\leq w}(\mathbf A^1_{Y_0})$.
